title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues p.749, where Grothendieck lists axioms 1°–4° for a 'linear/adelic realization' of a profinite LT-group M. M contains a profinite group π, for instance something like the completion of SL(2,Z) or of a Teichmüller-type fundamental group. π has a 'discretification' π_0, a discrete subgroup whose profinite completion is π.

The data are a continuous homomorphism ρ: M → G(A_Q), where G_Q is an affine Q-group scheme of finite type, together with a character χ_G: G → G_m. The axioms are:
1° Integrality: G extends to a finite-type affine group scheme over Z, and ρ factors through G(Ẑ).
2° Cyclotomic compatibility: χ_G∘ρ = χ_M, the cyclotomic-type character M → Ẑ^* (prime-to-p).
3° Compatibility with the discrete structure: on a finite-index subgroup π_0' of π_0, ρ takes values in G(Q).
4° (begun on p.749 and completed here) Minimality, i.e. 'irredundance': if G'_Q ⊂ G_Q is a closed subgroup scheme with ρ(M) ⊂ G'(A_Q), then G' = G.

The NB on this page: if 4° fails, there is a unique smallest G'_Q through which ρ factors. This is the 'adelic Zariski closure' of the image. Replacing χ_G by χ_G|G'_Q, the axioms 1°–4° hold for (G'_Q, χ') and M → G'(A_Q). So 4° is merely a normalization.

Remarque: let G_0 ⊂ M be the set of g ∈ M such that gπ_0g^{-1} and π_0 are commensurable. Equivalently, G_0 is the subgroup normalizing the 'germ of discretification' (the commensurability class) of π_0. This is the commensurator of π_0 in M. Grothendieck suggests strengthening 3° by requiring that ρ map G_0 into G(Q), not merely π_0'. He adds 'là-dessus le dictionnaire!', apparently a pointer to his Galois–Teichmüller dictionary. A margin note says G_0 plays the role of a discrete Galois or Teichmüller group.

On the next page (p.750) he reformulates: a distinguished subgroup Π with an L-structure, a discretification Π_0, and a discrete group 𝔊_0 ⊃ Π_0 normalizing Π_0 whose closure is normal in M. G_0 is thus the germ of the later 𝔊_0.

The overall aim appears to be an axiomatic notion of an 'arithmetic/motivic linear representation' of Galois–Teichmüller-type groups. In it, the discrete (topological, Teichmüller) side lands in Q-points, and the arithmetic side lands in adelic points with cyclotomic determinant.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'unique smallest G'' claim is correct and the justification is easy, though not written out. (G'∩G'')(A_Q) = G'(A_Q)∩G''(A_Q), since the scheme-theoretic intersection is a fibre product. Closed subgroup schemes of a finite-type Q-group satisfy the descending chain condition by Noetherianity. Hence the minimal G' exists and is unique.

Minor gap: after replacing G by the minimal G'_Q, axiom 1° needs a Z-model of G'. Take the schematic closure of G'_Q in the given Z-model G; then ρ factors through G'(Ẑ), because G'(A_Q)∩G(Ẑ) equals the Ẑ-points of that closure. Grothendieck's '...' glosses over this. It is routine.

The commensurator G_0 is a subgroup only if defined with care. With 'g π_0 g^{-1} commensurable with π_0' it is a subgroup. The handwriting 'g(π_0)' presumably means conjugation, or the action of g on π.
Strengthening 3° to G_0 → G(Q) is stated only as a possibility ('il est possible qu'il faille'). It is not justified, and its compatibility with 4° and with the existence of examples is not examined.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of an adelic linear representation of a profinite Galois/Teichmüller-type group M → G(A_Q). The axioms are integrality through G(Ẑ), cyclotomic determinant, Q-rationality on a discretification, and minimality.
ideas.modern_name: Compatible system of ℓ-adic (adelic) representations with motivic-type rationality conditions; algebraic/Zariski monodromy group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (abelian ℓ-adic representations, 1968); Deligne; Fontaine–Mazur philosophy
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in La Longue Marche (1981); this exact axiom list does not appear in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Unique smallest algebraic subgroup through which the representation factors, used to normalize the axioms (irredundance).
ideas.modern_name: Zariski closure of the image / monodromy group

ideas.what: Commensurator G_0 of the discretification π_0 inside the profinite group M, seen as the normalizer of the 'germ of discretification'. Grothendieck proposes that it should map to G(Q) and that it plays the role of a discrete Galois or Teichmüller group.
ideas.modern_name: Commensurator of a lattice / of a discrete subgroup in its profinite completion; Hecke-type symmetries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Commensurator of lattices and the arithmeticity criterion: Margulis (1970s). Hecke operators via the commensurator of SL2(Z) (Shimura). Discrete versions of GT: Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme speaks of the Teichmüller tower and of Galois–Teichmüller theory, but I do not know a published text with this commensurator formulation

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that the commensurator of the discretification π_0 inside the profinite Galois–Teichmüller-type group M should map into the rational points G(Q) of the realizing group. He calls it a 'discrete Galois or Teichmüller group'. This is a profinite-side analogue of the Margulis/Hecke picture, in which the commensurator of an arithmetic lattice is the group of Q-points. The idea is that the discrete symmetries visible from the profinite Galois action on a Teichmüller-type group should be arithmetic, i.e. Q-rational. Read this way, it suggests a discrete subgroup of GT-type groups singled out by commensurating a discrete mapping-class group. I am not aware that this has been systematically developed.
missed.quote: Soit G_0 ⊂ M le sous-groupe de M formé des g ∈ M qui sont tels que g(π_0) et π_0 soient commensurables ... Il est possible qu'il faille renforcer la condition 3°, en exigeant qu'on ait G_0 → G(Q). [marge] G_0 joue le rôle d'un groupe de Galois ou Teichmüller discret
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links commensurators (Margulis arithmeticity, Hecke operators) with Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory and the search for discrete or motivic avatars of GT. Profinite rigidity and commensurators of mapping class groups in their profinite completions are active topics.

missed.claim: Within Galois–Teichmüller theory, the axioms 1°–4° are an early attempt to define an adelic 'motivic realization' of the GT/Galois group acting on profinite mapping class groups. The arithmetic part goes to adelic points with integral structure and cyclotomic character, and the discrete topological part goes to Q-points. This anticipates later work on motivic or pro-unipotent realizations, such as Deligne–Ihara on Lie algebras and Brown on mixed Tate motives and GT, but in a profinite-adelic rather than pro-unipotent setting.
missed.quote: tel que M → G(A_Q) se factorise par G'(A_Q), alors G = G'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an alternative, adelic and reductive-flavoured framework for realizations of GT. The literature mostly uses pro-unipotent or ℓ-adic completions.

deep.surprise_reason: The minimality NB is routine. The Remarque proposing the commensurator of the discretification as a 'discrete Galois/Teichmüller group' that should land in G(Q) is a suggestive, apparently unpublished idea connecting commensurators and arithmeticity with Galois–Teichmüller theory. It remains a tentative sketch.

'{+long[?]+} cie[?] qui normalisent' is probably 'commensurables, (c.à.d.) qui normalisent le germe de discrétification'. The superscript word is unclear, perhaps 'longs' or 'lorsque'.
Margin: likely 'G_0 joue un rôle de groupe de Galois ou de Teichmüller discret'.
